title: EIP-7906: Transaction Assertions via State Diff Opcode
description: An opcode that provides a mechanism to restrict the outcomes of transaction execution
author: Alex Forshtat (@forshtat), Shahaf Nacson (@shahafn), Dror Tirosh (@drortirosh), Yoav Weiss (@yoavw), Fredrik Svantes (@0xfredrik)
laymanDescription: Signing a transaction today means trusting code most people cannot read, with no way to state what it must not do. This proposal adds instructions that let a check run at the end of a transaction, see everything that changed, and cancel the whole thing if the outcome is not what was expected.
benefits: Lets users set enforceable limits on what a transaction may do, replacing blind signing
A failed check cancels the entire execution and cannot be bypassed by earlier frames
Multiple independent assertion providers can compose without coordinating with each other
tradeoffs: An assertion that checks too little gives users a false sense of security
A failed assertion still commits gas payment, so the user pays for a rejected transaction
Assertions scanning all events can be gas-exhausted by attacker-padded logs
